chunks: As for what Yūnus narrated from Samāʿah, he said:
I asked him about the owned slave who falsely accuses a free person. He said: “Upon him are fifty lashes.”
So the correct way regarding it also is what we mentioned in the first report, because Samāʿah has narrated that eighty lashes are obligatory upon him as the hadd, and we have already cited it.

key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكِ: the owned slave; a legally unfree person
key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ: eighty, referring here to the number of lashes in the other report
key_terms.جَلْدَةً: a lash or stroke in corporal punishment
key_terms.خَمْسُونَ: fifty, referring here to the number of lashes
key_terms.يَفْتَرِي: falsely accuses or fabricates a charge

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a slave who falsely accuses a free person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling concerning a mamlūk who falsely accuses a free person, mentioning a punishment of fifty lashes in the narration. The closing note reconciles this with an earlier report from Samāʿah indicating that the hadd is eighty lashes, showing juristic treatment of apparently differing narrations.
